entry.title: Meeting 13: working on representations
entry.content: In the previous two weeks we took some time to individually write on our blurbs on representations from our respective angles. We met in smaller groups to discuss details. Today we got back together to inspect this work and discuss how we should further proceed.

entry.title: Meeting 12: working on representations and guest lecture by Michael Hahn (U Saarbrücken)

link.title: Meeting 12: working on representations and guest lecture by Michael Hahn (U Saarbrücken)

entry.content: This week the last talk of our mini lecture series took place on Tuesday. We met with our guest speaker Michael Hahn from the University of Saarbrücken before and after the talk to discussion our joint interests.

entry.title: Meeting 11: working on representations
entry.content: In our discussion today we went back to Markus Werning’s semantic assumptions (and the N400 effect and how it is interpreted) as well as with a review of our discussion from last week. We then discussed his mininal traces theory again and how all of this overall links to our topic of representation.

entry.title: Meeting 10: working on representations and guest lecture by Markus Werning (U Bochum)

link.title: Meeting 10: working on representations and guest lecture by Markus Werning (U Bochum)

entry.content: We continued our discussion on representations and worked on the draft individually. We also got prepared for our next invited guest speaker Markus Werning from the University of Bochum. His talk was very inspiring and so was the very intensive discussion with him on Thursday. A lot of food for thought!

entry.title: Meeting 9: working on representations
entry.content:
This week we continued our discussions on representations. Wolfgang provided some input and text that we have started to work on together. We also went to the next meeting of the research focus area “Learning individuals, organisations, societies and cultures” and formed a group that shares interests in the topics of competences, decision making and humans and AI.

For more information about our mission, visit our About page.

entry.title: Meeting 8: working on representations and guest lecture by Marcel Binz (Helmholtz Institute München)

link.title: Meeting 8: working on representations and guest lecture by Marcel Binz (Helmholtz Institute München)

entry.content:
This week we continued to discuss our project on representations. First, we had a feedback round on Colin’s talk and discussion and drew some conclusions. Then we identified key words and recurring topics, also delving deeper into the nature of representations by reflecting more on the philosophical side of things (what’s a model? computation? etc.) We also got prepared for the talk of our next guest speaker Marcel Binz from the Helmholtz Institute for Human-centered AI.

For more information about our mission, visit our About page.

entry.title: Meeting 7: working on representations and guest lecture by Colin Phillips (U Oxford)

link.title: Meeting 7: working on representations and guest lecture by Colin Phillips (U Oxford)

entry.content:
This week’s meeting was the first meeting after our two-week Easter break. On Monday we listened to the super interesting talk of our colleague Colin Phillips that we invited to our CSI lecture series. The topic was “Specific and general mechanisms in real-time linguistic computation” which also tackled the concept of (linguistic) representations. We continued our discussion on the topic on Tuesday and got the impression that Colin gave us a lot of food for thought for our enterprise.

For more information about our mission, visit our About page.

entry.title: Meeting 6: working on representations
entry.content:
This week, we finally came back to our discussion on representations. We had a lively debate on recurring questions that we identified in our different approaches to representation:

  • What are (mental) representations?
  • How are representations structured?
  • What is the content of representations?
  • Are representations observable or latent?
  • What are the function(s) of representations?
  • How are representations grounded?
  • What is the relation of representations to the external world?
  • Is research in your field possible without reference to representations?

Based on these recurrent questions, we tried to sketch a model that identifies different levels of representation. We aim to further flesh this out to provide a taxonomy that allows us to capture different aspects and/or theoretical assumptions that we and our respective fields make. We also plan to discuss these questions in more details with our guests that we will welcome in the weeks after the Easter break.

For more information about our mission, visit our About page.

entry.title: Meeting 4: working on our joint proposal

link.title: Meeting 4: working on our joint proposal

entry.content:
This week, we reserved the day for intensive, collaborative work on the proposal. We had all done our homework and delivered our parts for the projects and were thus able to effectively bring all of it together. We went for lunch to a really nice place round the corner (Sleepy Bird right at the Schillerpark) and then continued to work on the proposal. Charles joined us again in the afternoon and it all went well. At the end of the day we patted each other on our backs and were quite content.
